title: Hover to measure should outline the button or row you are pointing at, not the text inside it
goal: With the Measure tool, hovering an element on a screenshot is supposed to outline it and show its width and height. Today it only works when the element is empty: hovering a button reads nothing, hovering a toggle reads a 12 by 12 sliver of its knob, and hovering a settings row stops at the label text. Make hovering read the element a person would say they are pointing at.
notes: Diagnosis in queue/audits/2026-08-23-measure-redline.md. ElementBounds.detect walks outward and takes the NEAREST accepted EdgeMap candidate per direction, so glyph strokes win over the element boundary; over text the probe-side landings invert (minY > maxY) and it returns nil, which is why buttons read nothing. Measured counterexamples: strongest-edge-per-direction nails the button (233/480/755/815 -> 124x30 exactly) but makes a settings row grab its whole card (card bottom strength 1.0 beats the hairline divider at 0.795). Nearest-with-strength-threshold at 0.8 of the walk max fixes the button and still breaks the row. Likely needs a signal the edge map alone does not carry (uniformity beyond the candidate edge, or reusing FloodFill/ContourTracer from the wand). PhotonzCore has no image access today, so this may mean moving detection or passing a sampler in. Spec: docs/design/next-measure.md section 3.
acceptance: On the audit capture at queue/audits/2026-08-23-measure-00-capture.png, hovering the Save Changes button reads 124 by 30 logical px
Hovering a toggle reads 42 by 24, and hovering a settings row reads 624 by 44
Hovering a flat background area still shows nothing at all
A fixture-based unit test pins all four of those cases so the heuristic cannot regress silently
